# `start_view_star_sleep`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Start the Sleep view stage (view stage 4) on the open camera.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / probable (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xc94b0 (64-bit build), StartViewStarStage @0x3c1570; Sleep emission from ViewFunc sleep stage @0x3c5d64 |

No request parameters are read. If the view thread is already running stage 4 the call succeeds without restarting. Otherwise it requires an open camera, stops any current view, sets stage 4 and view mode 0, clears the camera subframe, selects page 0 and starts a named view thread, then returns without waiting for the stage to finish. On failure the reply carries the thread-local error code (207 when none was set). The stage reports through the Sleep function-state event, with working on entry, then cancel when a new view or stop request ends it (internal code 253, not sent), otherwise complete or fail. The stage only waits, in 60-second steps, while it runs. Emission READ; state-name mapping INFERRED.

Side effects: Stops the current view, resets view mode and camera subframe, switches the displayed page and starts the Sleep view thread. Blocking time of the prior view stop is not established.

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"start_view_star_sleep"`. [READ] |
| `params` | any | no | - | Not read. Omission, null, object, scalar and array all take the same path. Clients SHOULD omit it. [READ] |

| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |

The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 318 | The camera is not open | `device not connected` |
| 212 | The named view thread could not be created | `fail to create thread` |
| 207 | The helper failed without assigning a code | `fail to operate` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Other codes propagated from camera, page and thread helpers may occur; that set is unresolved.

## Example

Request, start:

```json
{"id":61,"method":"start_view_star_sleep"}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"start_view_star_sleep","result":0,"code":0,"id":61}
```

Reply, error:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"start_view_star_sleep","error":"device not connected","code":318,"id":62}
```
